introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (headed "One hour 30 minutes" on page 2): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (40 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (50 minutes): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A pupil photographer is told that to get photographs of the same size from objects of different sizes, the photographer has to move towards or away from the object thereby adjusting the distance between the object and the lens of the camera or the distance of the lens from the screen has to be adjusted with the distance of the object from the lens remaining constant.

Taking the second option, the student investigates how the distance, $d$ of the lens from the screen can be adjusted to obtain pictures of the same size using objects of different heights, $h_0$. The following data was obtained.

| $h_0$ / cm | $d$ / cm |
|---|---|
| 15.0 | 22.5 |
| 16.1 | 22.0 |
| 18.1 | 21.2 |
| 20.5 | 20.5 |
| 23.9 | 19.7 |
| 29.6 | 18.8 |
| 37.5 | 18.0 |
| 45.0 | 17.5 |
| 62.5 | 16.8 |
| 93.8 | 16.2 |

The two quantities above are related by the equation

$$d = f\left(\frac{h_i}{h_0} + 1\right)$$

where $f$ is the focal length of the lens and $h_i$ is the fixed height of the image formed in each case.
incertitudes: Question 7 : le graphe (a) est à tracer par le candidat ; le corrigé donne la grandeur à porter en abscisse (1/h0), le tableau des valeurs, les échelles et la lecture de l'ordonnée à l'origine, sans produire de figure de corrigé. Les dix points sont parfaitement alignés (f = 15,0 cm, pente 112,5 cm2, h_i = 7,50 cm).
Question 7 : marques imprimées 10 + 7 + 3 = 20, conformes au « Total 20 marks ».

questions.enonce_markdown: Plot a suitable graph from which $f$ and $h_i$ can be calculated. *[10 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Choosing the graph.** Expand the equation: $d = f h_i\cdot\dfrac{1}{h_0} + f$. This has the form $y = mx + c$ with $y = d$ and $x = \dfrac{1}{h_0}$. So plot **$d$ (vertical axis) against $\dfrac{1}{h_0}$ (horizontal axis)**: a straight line with **gradient $= f h_i$** and **intercept on the $d$ axis $= f$**.

**Table of values** (to be calculated by the candidate):

| $h_0$ / cm | 15.0 | 16.1 | 18.1 | 20.5 | 23.9 | 29.6 | 37.5 | 45.0 | 62.5 | 93.8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $\dfrac{1}{h_0}$ / $10^{-2}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$ | 6.67 | 6.21 | 5.52 | 4.88 | 4.18 | 3.38 | 2.67 | 2.22 | 1.60 | 1.07 |
| $d$ / cm | 22.5 | 22.0 | 21.2 | 20.5 | 19.7 | 18.8 | 18.0 | 17.5 | 16.8 | 16.2 |

**The graph (to be drawn by the candidate).** Axes labelled $\dfrac{1}{h_0}/\mathrm{cm^{-1}}$ (or $10^{-2}\,\mathrm{cm^{-1}}$) and $d/\mathrm{cm}$; scales that use more than half of each axis, starting the horizontal axis at $0$ so that the intercept can be read (for example horizontal $0$ to $7\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$ with $1\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$ per large square; vertical $0$ to $24\ \mathrm{cm}$). All ten points are plotted accurately; they lie very close to a single straight line (correlation coefficient $0.99999$), a best-fit line is drawn through them and **extended to the $d$ axis**, where it meets it at $d = 15.0\ \mathrm{cm}$.

**Focal length:** $f$ is the intercept on the $d$ axis (where $1/h_0 = 0$): $f = 15.0\ \mathrm{cm}$.

**Gradient:** use a large triangle on the best-fit line, for example the points $(6.67\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}},\ 22.5\ \mathrm{cm})$ and $(1.07\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}},\ 16.2\ \mathrm{cm})$:

$$\text{gradient} = \frac{22.5 - 16.2}{(6.67 - 1.07)\times10^{-2}} = \frac{6.3}{5.60\times10^{-2}} = 112.5\ \mathrm{cm^2}\ (\approx 113\ \mathrm{cm^2})$$

**Image height:** gradient $= f h_i$, so
$$h_i = \frac{\text{gradient}}{f} = \frac{112.5}{15.0} = 7.50\ \mathrm{cm}.$$

**$f = 15.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ and $h_i = 7.5\ \mathrm{cm}$.** (A least-squares fit of the ten points gives $f = 15.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ and gradient $112.5\ \mathrm{cm^2}$. Check on one point: $d = 15.0\,(7.5/20.5 + 1) = 20.5\ \mathrm{cm}$ for $h_0 = 20.5\ \mathrm{cm}$, as in the table.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is the name given to the ratio $\dfrac{h_i}{h_0}$?

(ii) Determine the value of $d$ when $h_i = h_0$? *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) $\dfrac{h_i}{h_0}$ is the **linear (lateral) magnification** $m$ of the lens: image height divided by object height.

(ii) When $h_i = h_0$, the ratio is $1$ (magnification of 1, image the same size as the object):
$$d = f\,(1 + 1) = 2f = 2\times15.0 = 30.0\ \mathrm{cm}.$$

**$d = 30.0\ \mathrm{cm}$.** This is the case $u = v = 2f$: the object and the screen are each at a distance $2f$ from the lens.
